title: Acquisition year matched breast-thermography model discrimination
summary: On a held-out set of 52 patients, acquisition year alone separated normal and sick labels with an AUROC of 0.974, within the range of the trained imaging models. On a separate 24-patient test set, confidence intervals for benign-versus-malignant classification all included chance.
ai_technology: BiomedCLIP, general CLIP variants and ViT-B/16; federated training simulation
organization: Southern Illinois University; Loyola University Chicago; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

evidence.tested: The authors separated patients across splits, tested acquisition year as a metadata-only score and compared it with the image-model outputs.
evidence.unknown: Only two acquisition years included both normal and sick labels. These data cannot separate acquisition effects from pathology, and the small malignancy test does not establish clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The learned thermography classifiers supplied the scores audited against acquisition dates and evaluated on the pathology distinction.
